source_refs.note: Topic 28.2 (PDF 179); Figures 28.2 and 28.3 are redrawn. The book expands Rf as 'Retardation factor or Retention factor'; the lesson uses retardation factor. The pencil question is added for the baseline term.

blocks.text: Paper chromatography uses a solvent to separate a mixture into its components; the separation depends on the relative solubility of the components. The paper contains water held by its cellulose. A small spot of the sample is put on a pencil baseline near the bottom of the paper with a capillary tube, and the paper is dipped in a suitable solvent, which soaks up the paper; the solvent level must be below the spot. The solutes in the sample dissolve in the solvent to different extents: some are more soluble in the solvent (the mobile phase) and move up the paper, while others dissolve better in the water trapped in the paper (the stationary phase) and do not travel far. This difference in solubility separates the components.

Chromatography separates both coloured and colourless substances; colourless substances are made visible by spraying them with a locating agent that gives them a colour. One advantage of chromatography is that it needs only a very small quantity of the mixture.

blocks.title: Rf value
blocks.text: The Rf value (retardation factor) of a substance is the distance travelled by the substance divided by the distance travelled by the solvent (the solvent front), both measured from the baseline: Rf = x / y. It has no unit because it is a ratio, and it does not change under the same conditions (same solvent and temperature).

blocks.alt: Left: a covered tank with solvent at the bottom and a paper strip standing in it; the pencil baseline with the sample spot is above the solvent, and spots A, B and C have moved up to different heights below the dashed solvent front. Right: a strip with the starting point, a spot at distance x from it and the solvent front at distance y; Rf = x / y.
blocks.caption: Paper chromatography and measuring Rf (original diagram after Figures 28.2 and 28.3).
blocks.long_description: The solvent rises through the paper and carries each component a different distance. Measuring each spot's distance from the baseline and dividing by the distance the solvent front travelled gives its Rf value, which can be compared with known substances.
